close_reason: Tightened the existing doc on server_fail_from_backend with an emphatic 'intentionally discarded' note + cross-ref to bd:JMAP-jfia.22. Rename/migrate options rejected (264 call sites, workspace prefers non-breaking changes). The workspace sealed dep set excludes tracing so a built-in log line is not on the table — callers log explicitly at the call site.
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/handlers.rs:69-71 — function signature is:

    pub fn server_fail_from_backend<E: std::fmt::Display + ?Sized>(_err: &E) -> JmapError {
        JmapError::server_fail(SERVER_FAIL_INTERNAL_DESC)
    }

The function takes an error reference and discards it; the body
ignores the parameter entirely and returns a JmapError whose
description is always the static "internal error" string. The
discard is intentional — the doc comment explains this is the
defense-in-depth guard that prevents the backend error's Display
output from reaching the JMAP wire response.

What callers cannot depend on (and what callers may wrongly assume):

A reader of just the function signature reasonably assumes the
parameter is used:

    .map_err(|e| server_fail_from_backend(&e))

The pattern looks like "wrap this backend error in a serverFail
invocation". The signature suggests the error info is preserved
somehow (logged, stashed, included as a `cause`); the body proves it
isn't. The doc comment clarifies, but reviewers of consumer code
who do not chase the function definition will think the error is
captured.

What goes wrong when this stays as-is:

1. Consumers add tracing/logging at the call site assuming the
   error is also being logged "somewhere by the helper" and then
   are surprised when nothing appears in operator logs except the
   static "internal error" wire response.

2. Future maintainers writing per-method handlers in extension
   *-server crates copy the pattern blindly and don't add their own
   structured logging, leaving operator-visibility gaps.

3. The `?Sized` bound + generic Display parameter looks like
   information-carrying — consumers might pass complex error values
   expecting some attribute to be picked up.

Resolution paths (one is sufficient):

- Rename: `server_fail_internal() -> JmapError` (no parameter).
  Force the caller to log the backend error separately:
      .map_err(|e| {
          tracing::error!(error = ?e, "backend failure");
          server_fail_internal()
      })
  The renamed function makes the discard explicit.

- Keep the name, change the signature so the discard is visible:
  `pub fn server_fail_from_backend() -> JmapError` and remove the
  err parameter entirely.

- Keep the parameter but actually use it for structured logging:
  add an optional tracing::error!() call inside the helper, gated
  behind a `log` Cargo feature. (This adds a dep and is heavier.)

The current shape is functional but misleading. The first option
costs the least.
title: server_fail_from_backend signature accepts err: &E but discards — misleading API shape
